meta.torqueFooter: Where a component maker's printed spec differs from the value shown, the printed spec wins. Use a calibrated torque wrench.

steps.title: Unbox & inventory
steps.summary: Open the box and confirm every part and tool is present before you start.
substeps: Place the box on a clean, flat surface and open from the top.
Lift the frame out by the front triangle — never by the rear derailleur or cockpit.
Locate the parts kit: pedals, thru-axles, accessory pouch, and the printed torque card.
Tick each item off the checklist below before continuing.
warnings: Do not discard packaging until assembly is complete and verified.
commonMistakes: Lifting the bike by the rear derailleur can bend the hanger and ruin shifting.

steps.title: Remove protective packaging
steps.summary: Strip foam, zip ties, and frame protection without scratching the finish.
substeps: Cut zip ties carefully with the flush side of the cutters against the foam, not the frame.
Remove foam tubes from the down tube, fork legs, and chainstays.
Peel off any low-tack protective film; leave permanent frame protection (chainstay guard) in place.
Set the bike in a workstand if you have one, clamping the seatpost — never the frame tubes.
warnings: Never clamp a carbon frame tube in a workstand — clamp the seatpost only.
commonMistakes: Pulling zip ties tight against the frame before cutting can scratch the clearcoat.

steps.title: Install the seatpost & saddle
steps.summary: Set the aero seatpost to height and torque the saddle clamp — carbon, so torque matters.
substeps: Apply a thin film of carbon assembly paste to the seatpost where it enters the frame.
Slide the seatpost in and set it to your saddle height (mark it for next time).
Tighten the frame seatpost binder to the value printed on the binder (see callout — A2 to confirm before this guide ships).
Level the saddle and tighten the saddle clamp bolts evenly to 5–6 N·m.

torque.note: See printed value on frame binder — A2 to confirm

warnings: Carbon contact point — never exceed the stated torque.
Carbon assembly paste is required to prevent slipping at safe torque.
commonMistakes: Skipping carbon paste and then over-tightening to stop slipping — this cracks the post.
Tightening one saddle-clamp bolt fully before the other; alternate in small increments.

steps.title: Install the cockpit / basebar
steps.summary: Mount the aero basebar and extensions, then set headset preload with the top cap.
substeps: Fit the basebar to the stem and start all clamp bolts by hand.
Tighten the basebar clamp bolts evenly to 5–6 N·m in a cross pattern.
Set the extensions to your reach and tighten their clamps to 5–6 N·m.
Snug the compression top cap to 2–3 N·m to remove headset play — this sets preload, not clamping force.
Align the stem to the front wheel and tighten the steerer clamp bolts last.

torque.note: Sets headset preload, not clamping force

warnings: Carbon contact points — never exceed the stated torque.
commonMistakes: Cranking the top cap to clamp the stem — the top cap only sets bearing preload; the steerer clamp bolts do the clamping.
Forgetting to align the bar square to the front wheel before final torque.

steps.title: Install the front wheel
steps.summary: Seat the wheel in the fork dropouts, guide the rotor into the caliper, and tighten the thru-axle.
substeps: Make sure the brake pads are not contaminated; keep fingers and oil off the rotor.
Guide the rotor squarely into the slot between the brake pads as you seat the wheel.
Push the wheel fully into the dropouts so it is centred.
Thread the thru-axle in and tighten it to the spec printed on the axle or hub.
Spin the wheel and confirm there is no rotor rub; re-seat if it ticks.

torque.note: Tighten to the spec printed on the axle / hub

warnings: Keep brake fluid, oil, and fingers off the rotor and pads — contamination ruins braking.
commonMistakes: Forcing the axle before the rotor is aligned in the caliper, bending the rotor.
Not seating the wheel fully in the dropouts, leaving it off-centre.

steps.title: Install the pedals
steps.summary: Thread the pedals into the crank arms — the left pedal is reverse-threaded.
substeps: Grease the pedal threads lightly.
Identify left (L) and right (R) — they are stamped on the spindle.
Right pedal: thread in clockwise (normal direction) on the drive side.
Left pedal: thread in COUNTER-clockwise — it is reverse-threaded.
Tighten both pedals to 34.5–40 N·m.
hazards: The LEFT pedal is REVERSE-THREADED — it tightens counter-clockwise. Forcing it the normal way will strip the crank arm.
warnings: Cross-threading a pedal destroys the crank arm — start every thread by hand.
commonMistakes: Installing the left pedal the normal direction and stripping the threads.
Mixing up left and right — check the L / R stamp on the spindle.

steps.title: Drivetrain check
steps.summary: Confirm shifting works across the full range; electronic builds need a battery check.
substeps: Lift the rear wheel (or use a workstand) and turn the cranks by hand.
Shift through every gear, easiest to hardest and back.
Watch that the chain moves cleanly with no skipping or hesitation.
If shifting is off, the rear derailleur may need minor barrel-adjuster tuning — see your build's notes.
warnings: Keep fingers clear of the chain and chainrings while turning the cranks.

conditional.heading: Shimano 105 (mechanical) tuning
body: Fine-tune with the barrel adjuster at the rear derailleur or shifter.
If the chain hesitates shifting to a larger cog, turn the barrel adjuster counter-clockwise a quarter turn.
If it hesitates to a smaller cog, turn it clockwise a quarter turn.

conditional.heading: Shimano Di2 (electronic) check
body: Press the shift buttons — you should feel and hear the motor actuate.
Check the battery charge by holding the function button; the LED shows charge state.
Charge with the supplied Di2 charger if the LED is red.
Micro-adjust via the junction box / E-Tube app if the index is slightly off.

conditional.heading: SRAM AXS (electronic) check
body: Confirm the derailleur battery is charged — the LED flashes green when good, red when low.
Charge low batteries on the supplied AXS charger, or swap front/rear batteries.
Pair / micro-adjust with the AXS app if shifting is slightly off.
Press the function button and shift with the paddle to confirm response.

commonMistakes: Assuming a shifting problem is the derailleur when the rear wheel simply isn't seated straight from Step 5.

steps.title: Pre-ride safety check
steps.summary: Run an M-check, set tire pressure, and re-confirm every critical bolt before riding.
substeps: M-CHECK: starting at the front wheel, work the 'M' shape across the bike — front wheel, fork/headset, bars, frame, saddle, drivetrain, rear wheel.
Squeeze both brake levers — they should feel firm and the bike should not roll.
Set tire pressure with a gauge. Use the range printed on the tire sidewall — but if your rims are hookless, never go above the rim's maximum, even if the tire allows more.
Re-check the critical torques: seatpost binder, saddle clamp, basebar, extensions, thru-axle, and pedals.
Lift each wheel and spin it — listen for rotor rub or anything loose.
hazards: ZIPP HOOKLESS WHEELS: never exceed the maximum tire pressure printed on the rim. Zipp hookless road wheels are rated to a maximum of 72.5 psi (5.0 bar). Over-inflating a hookless rim can blow the tire off the rim. When the tire's max and the rim's max differ, always use the LOWER number.
warnings: Do not ride until brakes feel firm and all critical bolts are confirmed at spec.
Hookless rims require tubeless-compatible tires — do not fit a non-tubeless or hooked-only tire.
commonMistakes: Inflating to the maximum on the pump rather than the correct range.
Reading only the tire's max pressure and ignoring a lower hookless rim limit.

steps.title: First rides
steps.summary: Bedding-in matters — re-check critical torques after your first couple of rides.
substeps: Keep your first ride short and local; stop and listen for new creaks or rubbing.
After the first 2–3 rides, re-check the critical torques (seatpost, saddle, cockpit, pedals, thru-axle).
Bed in disc brakes with several firm stops from moderate speed in a safe area.
Register your bike and review the warranty info in your owner's manual.
warnings: Carbon parts can loosen slightly as they bed in — the post-first-ride re-check is not optional.
commonMistakes: Skipping the re-torque after the first rides, then chasing a creak that is just a loose bolt.
